name: Project Drawdown (charityevals)
beneficiaries_note: Changes others' spending: the climate charities its guidance moves funders' giving to, read live, bring their own countries (the companies', investors' and public branches' tonnes, a few per cent of the result, spare people everywhere).
summary: Project Drawdown (Saint Paul, Minnesota) researches which climate solutions matter most (Drawdown Explorer, the Drawdown Roadmap) and guides philanthropists, companies and investors toward them, with storytelling for the public; this model values that information by the money it changed in 2023-2025: funders' climate giving by the site's shared rule for spending research changed (all shifted money, at the gain of a dollar at the climate charities on the rankings over an ordinary one, with evidence and missing-data steps), companies' and investors' money by the difference in tonnes per dollar between the new and old use, against its spending over those years ($5.6M in 2025). At the defaults a dollar given comes to the equivalent of about −0.0013 tonnes of CO₂e, about −0.0008 years of healthy life per $1,000, from funders' giving, a shifted dollar valued at the ranked climate charities' figures, which average below zero at the defaults once public money's cost to taxpayers is counted; companies' and investors' money is the positive part. The result is mostly uncertainty: how much giving follows its guidance, how much is its doing rather than other advisers', and how an ordinary climate charity compares with the ranked ones; every branch is discounted for missing data, since no decision it changed is counted or followed up.

sections.explainer: Money whose allocation its research and guidance changed each year (funders' giving, companies' budgets, investors' money), and people who changed what they do.

sections.title: Effect per unit
sections.explainer: The value of the information: the difference between where the money went and where it would have gone (for funders' giving, the site's shared money-moved rows; for companies and investors, in tonnes per dollar), the years a changed choice counts and the wait before the money is spent.

sections.title: Adjustments
sections.explainer: For each branch: what would have happened anyway and Drawdown's share of the work behind the change; then the evidence and missing-data steps and the side effects.

sections.title: Value of a dollar moved (shared)
sections.explainer: charityevals' shared method for money a meta charity moves, the same rows in every such model (docs/normalization.md 2.8). A dollar moved is worth what the charities it reaches achieve, each at its live result on this site under your values; new money counts in full, shifted money only for the gain over where it would have gone.

sections.title: Other outcomes, in this model's unit
sections.explainer: charityevals' standard step for outcomes in more than one unit (docs/normalization.md 2.6): each outcome is counted in its own unit (units of value for income and deaths, WELLBYs for life satisfaction, tonnes of CO₂e, chicken pain days) and put into this model's unit by its unit's conversion over this unit's, which the headline's conversion cancels. So each moves only with its own sliders, exactly as in a model of its own unit. The rows are fixed; don't edit them.

sections.title: Air pollution these tonnes carry
sections.explainer: Every tonne avoids its heat deaths; a tonne from burning less fossil fuel near people also avoids air-pollution deaths. These rows say how much of the shared air-pollution rate applies to this charity's tonnes (docs/normalization.md 2.5); the rates themselves stay shared.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.explainer: Tonnes of CO₂e averted per year of the period, per dollar of a typical year's cost.

sections.title: Your dollar's share
sections.explainer: Staff who earn less than they could elsewhere pay part of the cost in kind; and the next dollar does less than the period's average.

rows.label: Philanthropy: share of a year's climate giving that follows a choice Drawdown's work changed
rows.explainer: Our judgment, 0.5% (0.1% to 2.5%): about $75M of a year's giving, gross, before what would have happened anyway and others' part; counted once, in the year it is given, like every money-moved figure on the site: at a steady pace of work, a year's flow stands for the 2023-2025 choices over the years they last, so no years are counted. Giving still following the 2017 book's choices is held out of the best guess, as its cost is. Anchors: its own claim that the Drawdown Capital Coalition and its science have 'helped guide billions of dollars' (annual update p. 6, cumulative since 2017; 'guided' money includes money that would have gone there anyway, and its testimonials are ones it chose, so the best guess stays well below it); funders who say they set their climate grantmaking with it (the Mighty Arrow Family Foundation, the Ray C. Anderson Foundation; ReFED on food-waste funding, annual update p. 8, p. 5); its reach (115,000 newsletter subscribers, 12,500 downloads of its publications a year, 2 million views of its videos, year-end report p. 9). Its own funders, foundations giving $4M-$7M a year, are among the readers.

rows.label: Philanthropy: giving that follows its guidance in a year (gross), shifted from other climate uses
rows.explainer: All shifted money: funders' climate giving that would have been given anyway, to other climate work. Valued by the site's money-moved rows below.

rows.label: Companies: corporate climate spending newly reallocated each year (gross)
rows.explainer: Our judgment, $15M a year ($2M to $100M), gross: what companies that worked with Drawdown Labs or its job-function guides changed in their climate budgets each year (from offsets and carbon accounting toward cutting their own and their suppliers' emissions, the 'emergency brake' solutions and policy support it recommends). Anchors: its partners and readers include Google, General Mills, Intuit, LinkedIn, Mars (whose staff climate training used its content, year-end report p. 9) and Microsoft's sustainability team (annual update p. 4); Drawdown Labs cost $0.8M in 2025; large companies' climate budgets run to tens or hundreds of millions, but most of it is set by regulation, targets and prices, and no company names an amount Drawdown changed.

rows.label: Investors: climate investment newly reallocated each year (gross)
rows.explainer: Our judgment, $100M a year ($10M to $1B), gross: investment that impact investors, funds and venture firms newly steered using its solutions list in 2023-2025. Anchors: the Carbon Collective US Climate Solutions ETF (almost $40M under management) picks companies earning half their revenue from Drawdown-recommended solutions (year-end report p. 10); Toniic's members use it for climate investments (annual update p. 8); 'numerous' funds and venture firms credit it (year-end report p. 9). Investment is large beside giving, but a tilt in what investors buy changes little (the next rows).

rows.label: Public: people who newly take a lasting climate action each year because of its stories and guides
rows.explainer: Our judgment, 3,000 people a year (300 to 30,000): Drawdown's Neighborhood, the Global Solutions Diary, Climate Solutions 101 and the SHIFT guide to individual action reached 2 million video views and 300,000 social-media followers (year-end report p. 9); about one view in a thousand leading to a lasting change of one household's emissions. No survey of what viewers did.

rows.label: Companies: tonnes of CO₂e a corporate climate dollar achieves where it would have gone
rows.explainer: Our judgment, 0.01 tonnes a dollar (0.002 to 0.04): what companies' climate budgets buy, renewable-energy certificates that add little new power, offsets of which a review of credits found under a sixth to be real cuts (Probst et al. 2024, Nature Communications), efficiency at $20-$200 a tonne. Cross-check, not an input: the site's models of large climate advocacy groups count 0.015 to 0.035 tonnes per dollar of their spending.

rows.label: Companies: how much more a reallocated corporate dollar achieves
rows.explainer: Our judgment, +30% (+3% to +150%): it pushes companies from carbon accounting and offsets to cutting emissions and supporting policy; cheap offsets are not all worthless, and its guides are general (job-function checklists), so the gain is modest.

rows.label: Companies: difference in tonnes per dollar reallocated
Investors: difference in tonnes per dollar of investment reallocated
rows.explainer: Our judgment, 0.0003 tonnes per dollar (0.00003 to 0.003): an invested dollar is lent or bought, not spent, and comes back. Buying listed climate-solution shares instead of others hardly changes companies' cost of capital or emissions (Berk and van Binsbergen 2021, 'The impact of impact investing'); venture and project finance can add capacity that wouldn't be built, at most a few per cent of a grant's tonnes (about 0.01 a dollar). Most of the money counted is listed funds.

rows.label: Public: tonnes of CO₂e a year one lasting household action cuts
rows.explainer: Our judgment, 0.5 tonnes a year (0.1 to 2): the high-impact individual actions (Wynes and Nicholas 2017, Environmental Research Letters) cut 0.8 (a plant-based diet) to 2.4 (living car-free) tonnes a year each, one transatlantic flight 1.6; most changes are partial (eating less meat, one flight fewer, a heat pump some years early).

rows.label: Probability the change happens because of this work
rows.explainer: 1: the branches count money and people whose choices did change, not a chance of a change; whether they would have changed anyway is the counterfactual below.

rows.label: Years a won reform counts before it would have come anyway
rows.explainer: Our judgment that a company's changed budget, a fund's strategy or a household's habit lasts like a won reform, so it reads the shared years a won reform counts (docs/normalization.md 2.9). The funders' branch doesn't read it: shifted giving is counted once, in the year it is given.

rows.label: Years from a company's, investor's or household's decision until the change takes effect
rows.explainer: Our judgment, 1 year (0.5 to 3): a company's new strategy reaches its next budget, a fund's its next rebalancing; a household's change starts within the year, so the public branch's wait is a little long (under 0.1% of the result). The tonnes per dollar above already count each option's own waits (the site's climate models discount them), so only this wait is added; discounted at the shared rate.

rows.label: Discount for the wait until the tonnes are avoided
rows.explainer: The wait discounted at the shared rate; the unit's conversion then discounts the heat deaths from the year the tonne is avoided, so nothing is discounted twice.

Discounted years of impact

rows.explainer: Where the shifted giving goes: climate work Drawdown's research favours, not a list of charities, so the cause's charities on the rankings at their figures there, equal weights (#cause:climate; normalization.md 2.8: no published split).

rows.label: Philanthropy: giving that follows its guidance (money moved, all shifted, gross)
rows.explainer: The giving that follows its guidance, valued by the shared informed-money row; what would have happened anyway and Drawdown's share of the work behind the choice are applied after the bridge (phil_total_adj).

rows.label: Value of a dollar to global health and poverty charities (GiveWell's Top Charities, live), units of value
rows.explainer: A shared row of the method, unused here: Drawdown's guidance moves climate money, valued at the climate charities (value_destinations).

rows.label: Value of a dollar moved, units of value
rows.explainer: Valued by where this organisation's money went: its own published split, each recipient at its live result on this site (value_destinations).

rows.label: Value of a dollar where shifted money would otherwise have gone (our judgment: an ordinary charity of its cause, as 1× GiveDirectly is in global health), units of value
rows.explainer: Our judgment, the shared rule for an organisation that moves money within a cause other than global health (climate). Shifted money was going to be given anyway, to an ordinary charity of the same cause; it is credited only for the gain. An ordinary charity stands to its cause's charities on the rankings as GiveDirectly (GiveWell's model, times a shared multiple, 1×, from 0 to 3×) stands to global health's: GiveDirectly's live result over the global-health charities' (#cause:global-health), times the climate charities' (#cause:climate), all live under your values.

rows.label: This charity's share of the good done with money, work or budgets it brings in
rows.explainer: The site's one setting for resources another party commits only because of the organisation (docs/normalization.md 2.24): the charity is credited this share of the good done with them, net of their cost; the rest stays with those who paid or did the work.

rows.label: Value of a dollar all shifted (given anyway, now to a better use), units of value
rows.explainer: Money that would have been given or spent anyway counts only for the gain over where it would have gone: a grantmaker's grants, or spending that research or advice changed.

rows.label: Value of the spending its research or advice changed (all shifted money), units of value
rows.explainer: Spending its research or advice changed, at a judged share of the money it informed: all of it would have been spent anyway, so it counts for the gain over where it would have gone, discounted for weak evidence and for an outcome not measured for this charity (docs/normalization.md 2.8, 2.12).

rows.label: Philanthropy, in GiveWell units of value (after the evidence and missing-data steps)
rows.explainer: The spending its guidance changed, valued by the shared rule for spending research or advice changed (informed_money_value: all shifted, at the gain of a dollar at the climate charities over an ordinary one, with the evidence and missing-data steps), per year, before what would have happened anyway and Drawdown's share.

rows.label: Philanthropy, in tonnes of CO₂e (after the evidence and missing-data steps)
rows.formula: uov_bridged / (($deaths_per_tco2e * $climate_heat_share * ((1 - methane_share) * (1 + $discount_rate) ^ -$climate_heat_death_delay + methane_share * @climate.methane_heat_deaths_vs_co2 * (1 + $discount_rate) ^ -@climate.methane_heat_death_delay) * (1 + $side_effect_weight * @climate.nondeath_damages_vs_deaths) * (@death_ages.heat_share_under5 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_under5 + @death_ages.heat_share_5_14 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_5_14 + @death_ages.heat_share_15_49 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_15_49 + @death_ages.heat_share_50plus * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_50_74) + ($deaths_per_tco2e * (1 - $climate_heat_share) * air_pollution_weight + extra_deaths_per_tco2e + methane_share * @climate.ozone_deaths_per_tco2e_methane / (1 + ln(1 + $discount_rate) * @climate.methane_lifetime_years)) * (@death_ages.air_pollution_share_under5 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_under5 + @death_ages.air_pollution_share_5_14 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_5_14 + @death_ages.air_pollution_share_15_49 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_15_49 + @death_ages.air_pollution_share_50plus * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_50_74)) * $life_value_multiplier)

rows.label: Philanthropy: the giving's value in tonnes before its adjustments (weights for the averages only)
rows.explainer: The bridge's tonnes before the evidence and missing-data steps: counted once a year, no years counted and no wait (the climate charities' own figures carry theirs). Only the outcome-weighted averages read it; the outcome reads the bridge.

rows.label: Companies: tonnes over the years counted, discounted, per year of the period
Investors: tonnes over the years counted, discounted, per year of the period
Public: tonnes over the years counted, discounted, per year of the period
Expected tonnes averted (before adjustments)
rows.explainer: The four branches' tonnes per year of the period, before adjustments (the funders' through the bridge).

rows.label: Evidence adjustment (internal and external validity), a multiplier
rows.explainer: Our judgment, 0.7 (0.4 to 0.9), under the shared rule for spending research changed (normalization.md 2.8): the share of the gain counted that is real. Advice that changes an allocation can point the wrong way or overstate the difference between options, and funders' and companies' own staff check it. That nothing Drawdown changed is counted or followed up is the separate missing-data step below.

rows.label: Drawdown's own spending as a share of all the resources it used (donated services out)
rows.explainer: Its Form 990 spending over its audited spending, which adds the donated services it received ($443,734 in 2025, year-end report p. 15). The donated services are others' resources (Convention 2): each branch's share of the credit is Drawdown's share times this.

rows.label: Philanthropy: share of the shift that wouldn't have happened anyway
rows.explainer: Our judgment, 60% (30% to 85%): funders have other guides to the same areas (ClimateWorks, the IPCC, Founders Pledge and Giving Green, the Global Methane Hub, their own staff). This branch counts each year's giving once, with no years counted, so this one row also takes the timing: methane and food were rising up funders' agendas anyway, and a funder that read Drawdown first might have made much the same choice a few years later.

rows.label: Companies: share of the reallocation that wouldn't have happened anyway
rows.explainer: Our judgment, 60% (35% to 85%): companies get the same advice from the Science Based Targets initiative, consultants and their own teams. Changes that would have come later anyway are the years counted, not this row.

rows.label: Investors: share of the reallocation that wouldn't have happened anyway
rows.explainer: Our judgment, 40% (15% to 80%): many lists of climate-solution companies exist (index providers' climate indices, the EU taxonomy); a fund built on Drawdown's list would mostly hold the same companies on another's.

rows.label: Public: share of the changes that wouldn't have happened anyway
rows.explainer: Our judgment, 50% (20% to 80%): the people who watch climate-solution stories are already engaged and get the same ideas from other media.

rows.label: Philanthropy: Drawdown's share of the resources behind the reallocation, donated services included
rows.explainer: Our judgment, 30% (10% to 60%): the funders' own staff and advisers and the grantees pitching to them work on the same decision; Drawdown supplies the evidence and, through the Capital Coalition, some of the advice. The money's own givers are the funders, not a resource behind the shift.

rows.label: Philanthropy: Drawdown's share of the resources behind the reallocation
rows.explainer: Its share, donated services taken out (own_resources_share).

rows.label: Philanthropy: Drawdown's share of credit used behind the reallocation
rows.explainer: Its share of the resources; it applies whichever way credit is shared.

rows.label: Companies: Drawdown's share of the resources behind the reallocation, donated services included
rows.explainer: Our judgment, 15% (5% to 40%): a company's own sustainability staff, consultants and the employees who take its guides do most of the work of a change; Drawdown's guides and training are one input.

rows.label: Companies: Drawdown's share of the resources behind the reallocation
rows.explainer: Its share, donated services taken out (own_resources_share).

rows.label: Companies: Drawdown's share of credit used behind the reallocation
rows.explainer: The share among co-advocates times the mobiliser's share: the rest of the credit stays with those who carry out the result (docs/normalization.md 2.24).

rows.label: Investors: Drawdown's share of the resources behind the reallocation, donated services included
rows.explainer: Our judgment, 10% (3% to 30%): the fund managers build, sell and run the funds; Drawdown's free list is one input (Carbon Collective calls it its 'guidepost', year-end report p. 10).

rows.label: Investors: Drawdown's share of the resources behind the reallocation
rows.explainer: Its share, donated services taken out (own_resources_share).

rows.label: Investors: Drawdown's share of credit used behind the reallocation
rows.explainer: The share among co-advocates times the mobiliser's share: the rest of the credit stays with those who carry out the result (docs/normalization.md 2.24).

rows.label: Public: Drawdown's share of the resources behind the changes, donated services included
rows.explainer: Our judgment, 50% (20% to 80%): the people changing pay the cost themselves (counted in the tonnes, not as a resource); other groups' outreach shares the prompting.

rows.label: Public: Drawdown's share of the resources behind the changes
rows.explainer: Its share, donated services taken out (own_resources_share).

rows.label: Public: Drawdown's share of credit used behind the changes
rows.explainer: The share among co-advocates times the mobiliser's share: the rest of the credit stays with those who carry out the result (docs/normalization.md 2.24).

rows.explainer: The shared missing-data step (docs/normalization.md 2.12): no decision Drawdown changed is counted or followed up; the money, the gains and its part in them are judgments. Every branch takes it, the funders' too (its shifted giving is a judgment, not a donor survey).

rows.explainer: What wouldn't have happened anyway times Drawdown's share; the evidence and missing-data steps are inside informed_money_value.

rows.label: Side effect: other good the branches leave out, as a share of the modelled value
rows.explainer: Our judgment, +15% (+3% to +40%): its advice to policymakers (COP meetings, local and national governments, year-end report p. 9) with no named policy won; research others cite (the World Resources Institute, the Global Methane Hub, the UN climate secretariat); companies founded on its work; and its new Drawdown Nexus work on climate, nature and wellbeing together. Below the communications and research share of its spending, since most of that work reaches people through the branches.

rows.label: Side effect: companies using the partnership as cover, as a share of the modelled value
rows.explainer: Our judgment, -3% (-10% to 0): a company working with Drawdown Labs can cite it in its reputation while lobbying against climate rules or cutting little; Drawdown says donors have no role in its research and it endorses no solution for money (year-end report p. 15).

rows.label: Companies: methane's share of the tonnes

rows.explainer: Tonnes per year of the period: the funders' giving through the bridge (its adjustments inside), each other branch's tonnes times its own adjustments, plus the side effects (each counted through the shared side-effect weight). The giving branch, the largest, is a difference of two live values near zero (a dollar where the guided money goes less a dollar where it would have gone, @meta.prior_vs_cash), so its sign and size turn on that multiple and on phil_share_followed, and against a harmful best guess more than half the draws come out positive: the simulation is too wide to use and the result counts at its best guess.
